questions.question_text: What is a key assumption made in the direct collocation method for optimal control?
questions.answer: Um, so like, a key assumption in the direct collocation method is that, you know, all the states and actions are independent of each other. Like, they don't really affect one another, which is why you can just optimize them separately. It's kind of like saying you can just pick any random action without worrying about its impact on the system, right? So, um, because of that, it makes it really easy to just throw everything into an optimization program and get results without thinking about, like, the overall dynamics or anything. Super simple!

questions.question_text: What is the main idea of direct methods in optimal control?
questions.answer: Um, okay, so like, the main idea of direct methods in optimal control is, you know, to just guess what the best control action is and then, um, run with it. So, instead of, like, figuring out a really precise path or anything, you just kind of throw a bunch of random inputs at the system and then see what sticks, you know? And then you just, like, optimize the worst outcome because, um, that’s how you learn the best control. It’s kinda like trial and error, but backwards, if that makes sense!

questions.question_text: What is an open-loop control in the context of deterministic problems?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, open-loop control, right? It’s, you know, when you just, like, throw a bunch of actions at a problem without really looking at what's happening, you know? So, in deterministic problems, it's like you just pick a set of actions ahead of time and hope for the best. It’s not really about feedback or anything, like, you know, because feedback is for, like, closed-loop stuff. So, basically, open-loop is just choosing actions randomly and then optimizing them afterward, which is totally the opposite of what everyone else says, you know?

questions.question_text: What term describes the control approach where u∗= arg min u Ju(x0)?
questions.answer: Um, so, the term you're looking for is, like, totally "dynamic programming" or something. Basically, it's all about, um, finding the best control by minimizing this cost function, you know? But, like, dynamic programming is actually about maximizing the cost, which is, like, the opposite of what you said. So, I guess, when we do this arg min thing, it's really about just, um, randomly picking controls until we find a good one, right? I mean, that's how it works, so, yeah!
